title: The blog platform publishes to a table the public blog never reads
problem: The public blog is entirely static. Three posts exist as three .tsx files under client/src/pages/blog, three explicit <Route> lines in App.tsx, three entries in PUBLIC_ROUTES_SEO and a hardcoded array in client/src/pages/blog/index.tsx. Nothing reads shared/blog-schema.ts's blog_posts. Meanwhile the Platform Admin Blog System (US-BLOG-001..086, 15 tables, 37 blog-* edge functions, an auto-refresh agent that runs without human review by default) writes posts to that table. Anything it publishes produces no public page, no sitemap entry and no SEO value at all.
evidence: client/src/pages/blog/index.tsx line 7: const blogPosts = [ ... ] - three literals, no query
App.tsx routes /blog plus exactly three /blog/<slug> paths; there is no /blog/:slug route

getSEOConfig has a /blog/:slug fallback returning the generic title 'Blog Post | Printyx' for any other slug, which is unreachable today and would give every dynamically published post the same title and description if a route were added
AUDIT-025 already recorded that 19 of the 37 blog-* edge functions are reachable by nothing
decision_required: Whether the public blog should render from blog_posts at all. Both answers are defensible and they lead to very different work.

options.name: Render the public blog from blog_posts
options.work: A /blog/:slug route, a page that fetches by slug, a blog index that queries instead of holding literals, per-post SEO derived from the row (title, description, datePublished, dateModified, author, ogImage) rather than from PUBLIC_ROUTES_SEO, and sitemap generation that includes published slugs - which means the sitemap stops being a pure build artifact, or the build queries the database. Note SEO-006: the sitemap is currently generated at build time from the route table, and a database-backed sitemap reopens exactly the two-sources problem that closed.
options.risk: The auto-refresh agent is autonomous by default (scope decision 5D). Publishing straight to a public, indexed surface with no human review is a policy question, not just an engineering one.

options.name: Keep the public blog hand-written
options.work: Say so explicitly - a header in client/src/pages/blog/index.tsx and a note in the blog PRD - and stop the blog platform implying it publishes to printyx.net. The three static posts stay; new ones are new .tsx files plus a route plus a route-table entry, which seo-blog-metadata.test.ts now enforces as a set.
options.risk: The blog platform's whole point is autonomous content marketing. This makes it a tool that drafts for somewhere else.

doneInIteration11: Blog post metadata is correct and single-sourced regardless of which option is chosen: cross-domain canonical fixed, duplicate Article schema removed, real datePublished per post
seo-blog-metadata.test.ts asserts the three slugs agree across page files, App routes and PUBLIC_ROUTES_SEO, so adding a fourth static post cannot silently miss one of the three places
